records.note: No trans-prisoner housing data found for Tuvalu within budget (adds: 0). Wikipedia full-text search ('Tuvalu transgender prisoner', 47 hits) returned no jurisdiction-specific article on trans-prisoner placement, special units, or solitary/segregation; top hits were unrelated to prison housing (e.g. Samoan footballer Jaiyah Saelua, generic LGBTQ-rights pages). Penal Reform International's Global Prison Observatory has no Tuvalu country profile (penalreform.org/global-prison-observatory/country/tuvalu/ returned HTTP 404 'Page not found'), and the Wikipedia article 'LGBTQ people in prison' contains zero mentions of Tuvalu. The base record documents criminalisation of male same-sex conduct (max 14 years) and no legal gender recognition — the legal context in which any trans prisoner would face housing by birth sex — but no source documents actual placement practice, special units, segregation, or any case/ruling on trans-prisoner housing for TUV; Tuvalu's prison system is tiny (population ~11,000) and the evidence base is thin.
